stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because the hilltop enclosure at Varsk yielded no hearths, storage pits, or household refuse, archaeologists long regarded it as a ceremonial ground occupied only ______, when scattered communities gathered there for midwinter rites. A recent soil study challenges that interpretation: phosphate and microcharcoal traces, distributed evenly through every layer of the deposit, indicate that people cooked and slept at the site in all seasons for generations, and the missing refuse more likely reflects habitual sweeping.
explanation: The blank belongs to the old view, and the soil study "challenges" that view. So start with what the evidence shows: people lived at the site "in all seasons for generations." Flip it. The view being challenged must be that the site was used only at certain times of year. The clause "when scattered communities gathered there for midwinter rites" confirms this, because it needs a word about timing that a once-a-year festival would explain. "Seasonally" is the word that occupation "in all seasons" directly contradicts. Read the full sentence back with the negative in place: the old view said seasonal use, and the evidence shows year-round use. That reversal holds.

A.why: You matched the blank to the soil evidence (year-round occupation over generations) and skipped the reversal. The blank sits inside the view the study "challenges," so it has to be the opposite of continuous. Also, "occupied only continuously, when communities gathered for midwinter rites" contradicts itself.

C.why: You picked up on "scattered communities gathered" and chose a word about who used the site rather than when. The evidence that overturns the old view is about timing ("in all seasons"), and nothing in the soil study disputes that groups used the site together. The challenge would not land on this word.

D.why: You probably saw that a reversal was needed but flipped the wrong feature. You read "distributed evenly through every layer" as a statement about space and looked for its opposite. Layers of a deposit record time, not area. The "when" clause after the blank also needs a time word, and "partially" describes space.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Managers of the Teller Basin long assumed that its springs drew on water that had percolated underground for thousands of years, so a dry year would trim their flow only slightly. Tritium measurements now complicate that picture: most of the spring water fell as rain within the past several decades, and discharge dropped by nearly half after the 2021 drought. The findings suggest that the springs are far less ______ short-term drought than managers had supposed.
explanation: First, say what the evidence shows: the water is young, and flow fell by almost half after one drought, so the springs are highly sensitive to dry years. The phrase "far less ______ than managers had supposed" means the blank must describe what managers wrongly believed, which is the opposite of sensitive. Now check how strong the managers' belief was. They expected a dry year to "trim their flow only slightly." That means they thought the springs were cushioned, not untouched. "Buffered against" matches that belief exactly. Read it back: the springs are far less buffered against drought than supposed, which is consistent with flow dropping by half.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (the springs are sensitive to drought) and skipped the "far less... than supposed" reversal. The sentence would then claim the springs are less vulnerable than thought, which is the opposite of what a nearly 50% drop in discharge shows.

C.why: You correctly saw the reversal but went to the strongest opposite. Managers never thought the springs were immune. They expected flow to drop "only slightly," which means they expected some effect. "Immune" overstates the view being corrected, and "far less immune" makes little sense, since immunity has no degrees.

D.why: You chose a word that fits the passage's groundwater topic (recharge, percolation) instead of the sentence's logic. Drought does not recharge springs, and the passage is about how strongly a dry year reduces flow, not about what refills the aquifer.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because maize and beans draw on the same shallow soil water, agronomists long expected intercropping the two to ______ maize yields in dry years. Three seasons of field trials in central Malawi did little to support that expectation: maize planted between rows of beans produced no less grain than maize grown alone, and in the driest of the three seasons it produced slightly more.
explanation: The blank is inside the expectation, and the trials 'did little to support' it, so the blank has to be the opposite of what the trials found. The trials found yields held up or rose, so the expectation was that yields would fall. The opening 'because' agrees: two crops competing for the same water would be expected to lower yields. 'Depress' means lower.

A.why: You noticed the reversal but stopped too early. 'No less grain' sounds like stable yields, so you went with that. But the expectation was supposed to follow from competition for water, and competition doesn't predict stable yields. It predicts lower ones. 'Stabilize' also describes what the trials found, and the expectation is meant to be the opposite of that.

B.why: You matched the blank to the result, since maize did slightly better in the driest year, and skipped the reversal. The trials 'did little to support' the expectation, so the expectation was the opposite of a boost.

D.why: You picked a word that sounds like how scientists talk about measurement. Nothing in the passage is about yields being hidden. The 'because' clause predicts a real effect on how much grain grows.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Historians once portrayed the hand-loom weavers of 1820s Lancashire as ______ mechanization. Guild account books complicate that portrait: many weavers paid to use power looms in the evenings, and some pooled their savings to buy the machines outright. The weavers' later protests, the books suggest, were aimed less at the looms themselves than at the wage cuts that mill owners introduced alongside them.
explanation: The account books 'complicate' the old portrait, so the portrait is the opposite of what the books show. The books show weavers renting and buying power looms, which means they took up the machines willingly. The old portrait was therefore that they opposed mechanization. The last sentence supports this: the protests that seemed to show opposition were really about wages.

A.why: You described what the account books show and forgot that the books 'complicate' the portrait. Because the blank sits inside the view being challenged, it has to be the opposite of the evidence.

C.why: Paying to use looms every evening sounds like being used to them, so you matched the evidence again. That's the same skipped reversal in a milder word. A portrait that the books 'complicate' can't also say what the books show.

D.why: You went for a word about the weavers' importance to industry. The passage is about how the weavers felt toward the machines, not whether the machines depended on them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: A vaccine that raises antibody levels in the blood does not necessarily ______ infection. The respiratory virus studied by Okafor's team multiplies in the lining of the nose, which blood-borne antibodies rarely reach. Vaccinated animals in her trials still carried and shed the virus, although they were spared the severe lung disease that developed in unvaccinated animals.
explanation: Start with what's true: vaccinated animals still carried and shed the virus, so they were still infected. The sentence says the vaccine 'does not necessarily' do the blank to infection, so the blank is what the evidence shows the vaccine failed to do. It failed to stop infection, so the answer is 'block'. The protection from lung disease is a separate point about how severe the illness was, not whether infection happened.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence (the animals did get infected) and didn't apply the 'does not necessarily'. Put it back in the sentence: 'does not necessarily permit infection' says the opposite of what the trials found.

B.why: You applied the negative, but to the wrong idea. Nothing suggests the vaccine might make infection worse. The animals were actually spared severe disease, and the passage is about whether the vaccine stops infection, not whether it worsens it.

C.why: You picked a word from the medical setting. Vaccines don't diagnose anything, and the evidence is about whether the virus got in, not whether anyone detected it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: The blank stretches of coastline on many sixteenth-century Portuguese charts have often been read as a sign that their makers were ______ the lands beyond them. Yet the same workshops covered other unvisited coasts in confident, invented detail whenever a patron requested it, so the empty stretches may record a deliberate refusal to speculate rather than a simple lack of information.
explanation: The blank is inside the reading that 'Yet' knocks down, and the last clause names what that reading was: 'a simple lack of information'. The new view is that the mapmakers chose not to guess. So the old view, the one in the blank, is that they didn't know. 'Uninformed about' matches that.

B.why: You described the passage's own new reading, that the mapmakers refused to speculate, and put it into the old view it replaces. The blank comes before 'Yet', so it has to be the opposite of where the passage ends up.

C.why: You read the blanks as hiding something. The passage pins down the old reading exactly: it was about 'a lack of information', not about withholding information on purpose.

D.why: 'Extravagant' describes the other coasts, the ones filled with invented detail. That's the opposite of a blank stretch, so it can't be how the blanks were read.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Critics have tended to dismiss the cadenzas in Ottilie Brandt's 1838 piano concerto as little more than ______ displays, opportunities for the young composer to show off her speed at the keyboard. Her sketchbooks tell a different story: she revised each cadenza many times, and several bring back themes from earlier movements in new keys, tying the concerto's three parts together.
explanation: 'Little more than' signals the critics' low opinion, and the phrase after the comma says what they meant: showing off speed. The sketchbooks 'tell a different story', showing the cadenzas hold the work together. The blank is the critics' word, so it has to mean decorative and surface-level. That's 'ornamental'.

A.why: You took the blank from the sketchbook evidence ('tying the concerto's three parts together') and missed that it sits inside the dismissive view that the sketchbooks overturn. Also, 'little more than unifying displays' isn't a dismissal at all.

B.why: You saw 'bring back themes from earlier movements' and read it as repetition. That detail is part of the evidence against the critics, not their complaint. The comma phrase says the critics thought the cadenzas were for showing off, not that they were borrowed.

D.why: You chose a word about tone. A display meant to show off a player's speed is flashy, not solemn, so it clashes with how the critics' own view is defined.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Because the dips in the brightness of the star Kessler-9 recur every 41 days with the same depth and duration, astronomers consider them unlikely to be ______. A drifting cloud of dust or a passing comet would block the star's light unevenly and at irregular intervals. The regularity of the dips instead points to a planet in a stable orbit.
explanation: What's true is that the dips are regular, repeating every 41 days with the same depth. 'Unlikely to be' reverses that, so the blank is the opposite of regular. The next sentence confirms it by describing dust and comets, which block light 'unevenly and at irregular intervals'. 'Erratic' means irregular.

A.why: You described the evidence (the dips repeat on a schedule) and left out 'unlikely to be'. Read the whole sentence: astronomers can't consider repeating dips 'unlikely to be periodic'.

C.why: You saw that the blank gets denied and grabbed the passage's conclusion to deny. But the last sentence says the dips do point to a planet. Calling them 'unlikely to be planetary' flips the reversal a second time.

D.why: You matched the topic, light from a star. The sentence is about the pattern of the dips over time, not how bright they are.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Lindqvist's analysis of borehole records challenges the view that the Varga Fault is ______, a structure that has already released its built-up strain and now poses little hazard. Since 1970, the records show, the two sides of the fault have stopped slowly creeping past each other. That stillness means strain is accumulating along the fault rather than being relieved.
explanation: The blank names the view that Lindqvist challenges, and the phrase after the comma defines it: a fault that has already released its strain and is no longer dangerous. 'Spent' means used up. The evidence points the other way. The fault has stopped moving, so strain is building up.

A.why: You matched the blank to Lindqvist's finding. The fault stopped moving, so it is locked. But the blank is the view she 'challenges', so it has to be the opposite of her finding. A locked fault building strain is the reverse of one that 'poses little hazard'.

B.why: You may have sensed the fault is dangerous and chosen a hazard word. But the phrase defining the challenged view says the fault 'poses little hazard', so 'unstable' contradicts the view it is supposed to name.

C.why: You picked a word from the geology setting. The passage never discusses depth. The view being challenged is about whether the fault's strain has been used up.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Radar records from the 2019 season make the afternoon sea breeze look less ______ than coastal forecasters had assumed. The breeze had long been credited with suppressing thunderstorms over the city by carrying in cool, stable marine air. Yet on most days that summer, the line where it pushed into warmer inland air was precisely where the first storms formed.
explanation: The radar shows the sea breeze setting off storms where it meets inland air. The breeze is 'less ______ than forecasters had assumed', so the blank describes the old belief, which the radar weakens. That belief, stated in the next sentence, was that the breeze held storms off. 'Benign' (harmless or protective) fits the old belief, and the radar shows the breeze is less harmless than people thought.

B.why: You matched the blank to what the radar shows, the breeze triggering storms, and didn't apply 'less'. Read it back: 'less disruptive than assumed' would mean it causes even fewer storms, which is the opposite of the finding.

C.why: You chose the breeze's most obvious feature. The passage never questions whether it brings cool air. The finding is about storms, not temperature.

D.why: You read the finding as being about how far the breeze reaches. Nothing in the passage says forecasters were wrong about its size. Their mistake was about what it does to storms.
